newsitem.title: USA: Galileo International files for public offering.
newsitem.headline: Galileo International files for public offering.

text.p: Galileo International Partnership, an electronic travel services company owned by several airlines, said Tuesday it filed an initial public offering plan with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

Separately, Galileo said it reached agreement with UAL Corp's United Airlines, US Airways Group In and Air Canada to buy the airlines' interests in Apollo Travel Services Partnerships for an aggregate purchase price of $700 million.
Galileo said its current 11 airline owners will each retain an ownership interest in the company.
A portion of the shares will be offered in the United States and a portion in a concurrent international offering.

Net proceeds from the primary shares to be issued in the proposed offering will be used by Galileo International to provide a portion of the financing for the proposed acquisitions of Apollo Travel Services from United Airlines, US Airways and Air Canada; Galileo Nederland B.V. from KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV ; and Traviswiss from Swissair AG.

ATS Galileo Nederland and Traviswiss are each national distribution companies for Galileo International's global distribution system products. Galileo International and the owners of each of these companies have reached non-binding agreements in principle, subject to definitive agreements and satisfaction of certain conditions.
In the Apollo acquisition, Galileo International said it may pay in the sixth year following the sale up to an additional $200 million on a present value basis to the airline owners.

"We believe that Galileo International's decision to acquire ATS (Apollo Travel) is a sound one, made in the best interests of all parties," James E. Barlett, president of Galileo International, said in a statement.
"Our combined resources will create an even more customer-focused organization that will enable us to better serve our customer base."
The transaction is subject to execution of definitive agreements and the satisfaction of certain conditions, including the successful completion of Galileo International's initial public offering.
United, US Airways and Air Canada currently own approximately 38 percent, 11 percent and one percent of Galileo International, respectively. Eight other international airlines own the balance.
Apollo Travel Services is a separate company of which United owns 77 percent, US Airways 21 percent and Air Canada two percent

Galileo provides travel agencies at approximately 36,000 locations as well as other subscribers with the ability to access schedule and fare information, book reservations and issue tickets for 525 airlines.
